name: @cloudsforge/activity
description: The bus tail, in one process. ACTIVITY: the canonical activity feed — subscribes to every domain topic and writes one immutable activity_record per user-visible event, written only from the event bus. NOTIFY (absorbed in wave M2): event to notification mapping, preferences, templates, dedupe, digests, retries, delivery history, operator broadcasts and developer webhooks as one pipeline. Two databases, two migrators, two module-labelled job runners with independent concurrency budgets, one listener, and one event-bus inbox per module because they authenticate with different secrets.

scripts._test: --test-concurrency=1 is required, not a preference: every database test file truncates between cases, and node:test runs FILES in parallel by default. A TRUNCATE takes an AccessExclusiveLock, so one file's reset deadlocks against another file's inserts (40P01).

_localDependencies: The @cloudsforge/* packages are consumed from sibling checkouts because none of them is
published yet. Once AD-02 lands they all become registry versions and these paths are deleted.
The runtime packages take 'file:' and the contracts packages take 'link:'. The difference is
not cosmetic: a contracts package may depend on another with the 'workspace:^' protocol, which
only resolves inside the contracts workspace. 'file:' packs the directory and honours
files: ['dist'], which installs a package whose exports point at sources that were not packed.
'link:' symlinks the package in place and lets it keep using its own node_modules.
tsx is a runtime dependency for the same reason: the unpublished packages resolve to their
@cloudsforge/contracts-chain is a RUNTIME dependency and not a dev one, for the same reason
micro-notify's is: classify.ts asks it a question while classifying — RETIRED_ASSETS, so that
no summary can name a wound-down asset to a player whatever a producer sends (micro-org #227).
A guard that only existed under `pnpm test` would not be a guard.
nodemailer arrived with wave M2 and is a RUNTIME dependency, imported LAZILY and only once
SMTP_HOST is set. An unconfigured transport is a supported mode (see src/notify/email.ts), so
the module must not be needed to boot a deployment that sends no mail.
